narrative.overview:
The Civic Dispatch embodies reliable, trustworthy, civic-minded utility balancing municipal clarity with modern digital efficiency. Built for tier-2 commerce ecosystems like Panipat, where the pilot starts, Kovera’s visual world communicates institutional dependability without bureaucratic inertia, and marketplace speed without predatory gig-economy detachment.

The visual language is grounded in approachable, dependable, and civic optimism. Generous tactile forms (12px inputs, 16px buttons, 24px cards, and full-radius pill tags) convey welcoming neighborhood warmth. Dual-sided architectural balance grants equal visual weight and dignity to local business owners and ready-to-work individuals.

Kovera deliberately rejects the cold, sterile data grids of corporate gig apps and the hyperactive visual clutter of promotional classifieds (loud flashing badges, neon starbursts, abrasive discount stickers). Every surface maintains daylight readability, generous breathing room, and tranquil, high-contrast clarity.
keyCharacteristics: Dual-Sided Marketplace Symmetry: Structural pairing of Deep Civic Indigo for business needs and Worker Cyan for worker opportunities.
Flat Tonal Layering: Subtle tinted card surfaces (#EEEFFC and #E0F7FA) with 1px hairline borders; no shadows, gradients or decorative shapes.
Tactile Ergonomics: Pill badges, friendly rounded containers, and 44px-minimum controls make participation welcoming and frictionless.
High-Integrity Clarity: Strict avoidance of hype, opaque tech terminology, or false urgency.

rules.name: The Dual-Sided Symmetry Rule
rules.body: Business elements must never use Worker Cyan as their primary fill, and worker elements must never use Civic Indigo as their primary fill. Color serves a structural role separating demand from supply, never a purely decorative one.

rules.name: The Daylight Safety Rule
rules.body: Dark backgrounds are restricted to the navy sections (#201F53) and footer. General interactive forms and workflow surfaces must always operate on light canvas tones (#F7F8FC, #FFFFFF) to reinforce daytime safety and open commercial environments.

rules.name: The Scannable Clarity Rule
rules.body: Headings must never exceed three lines on mobile screens. Subheadings must deliver immediate operational context rather than abstract marketing fluff.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: All content cards, form containers, and lists remain flat, distinguished only by surface tint and 1px hairline strokes. The only shadows are on the floating WhatsApp button and the open mobile menu. No gradients, blurred background shapes or decorative animation.

dos: Do maintain strict visual symmetry between Business and Worker content blocks across all comparison surfaces.
Do use the Tailwind tokens from src/index.css (bg-biz, text-worker, border-line, text-body) instead of one-off color hexes.
Do keep cards flat at rest, with no shadows.
Do use one selected style everywhere: solid side colour, white text, check mark.
Do make every control at least 44px tall and keep informative text at 14px or larger.
Do frame all shifts around daylight hours (8 AM to 8 PM) and public commercial workspaces.
Do write concise, scannable microcopy with explicit ₹0 worker guarantees.
donts: Don't use flashy discount banners, sticker badges, or countdown timers that evoke spam classifieds.
Don't mix business indigo and worker cyan within the same component button or badge.
Don't use worker-bright for text; it is for icons, the logo dot and accents.
Don't use gradients, blurred background shapes, backdrop blur, uppercase labels or letter-spaced labels.
Don't use pure black (#000000) for text or backgrounds; always use Ink Navy (#181A32) or Midnight Indigo (#201F53).
Don't introduce dense, enterprise-style data tables without mobile card fallbacks.
Don't hide or obscure the Phase 0 pilot disclaimer; transparency is core to building local trust.
